WakeForce
Field guide · v1.0 · Dark edition

Your alarm doesn't stop
until you've solved it.

WakeForce is an alarm clock for JEE aspirants. There is no snooze and no dismiss button — the only way to silence it is to answer a JEE-level question. By the time the room is quiet, you are already awake and already thinking.

  • 06:00 Alarm rings → solve to stop it
  • 08:00 Routine block starts
  • 08:00 Focus shields your distractions
  • 22:00 Progress shows what you actually did
The whole idea

What happens at six in the morning

This is the whole product in two screens. Every other feature exists to support it: the routine tells you when to study, focus keeps you there, and progress shows whether any of it stuck.

Start here

Installing it

  1. Open the APK you were sent and tap Install.

    WakeForce isn't on the Play Store yet, so your phone will want a moment of convincing.

  2. If it says “App not installed”, tap More details → Install anyway.

    Android says this about any app that doesn't come from the Play Store. It isn't a fault in WakeForce.

  3. Allow “unknown apps” for whatever you opened the file from — WhatsApp, Files or Chrome.

    Once only.

  4. Open WakeForce and sign in with Google.

    That ties your streak and XP to you rather than to the phone.

One-time setup

Four permissions, and what each one buys you

WakeForce asks for these on the screen where they're used, never all at once. Skip any and the app still runs — that part just stays off.

PermissionAsked onWithout it
Full-screen notificationsBanner at the top of Alarms The alarm arrives as a notification you must tap, instead of taking the screen
Usage accessFocus → Shield apps Focus can't tell which app you opened, so nothing is shielded
Draw over other appsFocus → Shield apps Focus sees the distraction but can't cover it
Do Not Disturb accessFocus → Do Not Disturb The phone stays audible during a session
Do this one first

Grant full-screen notifications before anything else. Without it the alarm waits politely to be tapped, which rather defeats the point of an alarm. On OPPO, Realme, Xiaomi and OnePlus phones, also allow WakeForce to run in the background — those phones freeze apps aggressively.

The core loop

Setting an alarm you can't dismiss

Open Alarms, tap + bottom-right, and set the time on the dial — it scrolls round, so you can spin past 12 straight back to 1. Check AM/PM before saving; the app tells you exactly when it will next go off, so read that line.

Then pick the mission. At the chosen time the alarm rings and the only control on screen is Solve to stop alarm. Volume, dismiss and snooze do nothing until the question is answered. Wrong answers cost you thirty seconds.

You get five alarms. Routine blocks don't count against that.

Missions

What wakes you up

Every question is JEE-level — Mains through early Advanced, not textbook recall. The app never repeats a question you've already answered correctly, so the bank keeps moving forward with you.

Maths

Calculus, sequences, matrices, probability, coordinate geometry.

322 questions

Mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, modern physics.

318 questions

Chemistry

Physical, organic and inorganic, including solid state and coordination.

322 questions

Shake

No question — shake the phone until it's satisfied. For mornings you genuinely can't think.

Your day

Routine blocks

A routine block is a piece of your day with a name and a time — Physics 08:00–10:00, Lunch 13:00–14:00, Gym 17:00–18:00. Open Alarms → Routine and tap +.

Each block can do three things: remind you a few minutes early, ring as a full alarm so it can't be ignored, and — for a study block — start a focus session the moment it begins.

When a block rings you get three choices: start the focus session, snooze five minutes, or skip today. Unlike the wake alarm, a routine block lets you walk away. Only the morning one locks the phone.

A routine alarm is tinted to its subject — Physics blue, Chemistry green, Maths orange — so you know what's starting before you've read a word.

Break and personal blocks behave differently: a lunch block asks you to step away from the desk, and a gym block offers to silence your phone rather than start a study timer.

While you study

Focus mode

Pick what you're sitting down for, choose Goal (a fixed number of minutes) or Open (count up until you stop), and start.

While it runs, Shield apps watches what comes to the front. Open Instagram and a full-screen panel covers it until you go back to studying. Do Not Disturb silences the phone, with one deliberate exception: if the same number calls twice within fifteen minutes it rings through, so a parent can always reach you.

At the end you get the honest version of the hour — minutes actually sat, how close you came to your goal, and which apps pulled at you, by name and with counts.

Over time

Progress

Your streak counts consecutive days you woke and solved the mission. Miss a day and it resets — that is the entire point of it.

XP comes from solved missions and focus minutes, and levels you up from Sleepy Starter onward. Questions solved is split by subject, so you can see which one you have been quietly avoiding.

Where a number has nothing behind it yet, the app shows a dash rather than a zero or a flattering percentage. A statistic you can't trust is worse than no statistic.

Two minutes on Alarms

A good first setup

  1. One wake alarm at the time you actually want to get up.

    Maths or Physics, Medium. Two questions wakes you without being cruel at 6am.

  2. Two study blocks for the parts of the day you already study.

    Turn on Ring as full alarm for the one you skip most often.

  3. Shield the three apps that actually cost you time.

    Three, not everything. A shield you resent gets switched off by Wednesday.

  4. Check Progress on Sunday.

    Once a week. The numbers are there to be read occasionally, not watched.

If something looks wrong

Questions

My alarm made a sound but didn't open on screen

Android blocks full-screen alarms by default. Open Alarms and tap ALLOW on the banner at the top. On OPPO, Realme, Xiaomi and OnePlus phones also allow WakeForce to run in the background — those phones freeze apps a few seconds after the screen goes off, which stops the alarm screen appearing.

“App not installed” when I try to install the APK

Tap More details → Install anyway. If there's no such option, open Play Store → Play Protect → Settings, turn scanning off while you install, then turn it back on.

Focus isn't blocking anything

It needs Usage access and Draw over other apps. Open Focus and tap ALLOW next to Shield apps — it asks for whichever is still missing, so you may need to tap twice. Both granted turns the row green.

My routine block never went off

Two usual causes. Check AM/PM — 12:30 at night and 12:30 at lunch are easy to confuse. And check the repeat days: a block only fires on days you selected. When you save one, the app tells you exactly when it will next fire. If that says next week, something is off.

Can I turn the alarm off from the notification?

No. That is the feature. Volume, dismiss and snooze are disabled until the mission is solved. If you genuinely can't answer, the Shake mission is the escape hatch — set that for mornings you know will be rough.

Does it work without internet?

Yes. Alarms, questions, routine and focus all run offline. You only need a connection for the first Google sign-in.
